reviewer.id: Claude subagent (fresh context, same model family as the builder)
reviewer.tools: Read tool on every evidence PNG; PIL crops and 1.6-2x upscales of ordered-frames.png tiles (written to the session scratchpad) to inspect small details such as shadow poses, eyes and the wink

opening_promise.note: The situation and feeling land at once: a round creature in a red stocking cap walks in from the right (0.5s), stops (2.0s) and sighs at a warm sunset (3.0s), and the framing gives its long shadow the whole lower half of the frame so it reads as a co-star; but the specific hook (the shadow copying one beat late) is a motion property I cannot see, and in the stills the first sure sign of the shadow acting alone comes at 5.0s, late for a scroller.
opening_promise.evidence: 0.00-3.00s (f0-f90); phone-f00048; first visible anomaly 5.00s f150 (shadow's arms still spread after Pim's arms are down)

progression.note: Each section changes the situation rather than listing gags: copying (0-3s), then the shadow holds the stretch, Pim does a double-take and the shadow snaps innocent (5.0-6.0s), then Pim tests it with arm raises (7.0-8.5s), it peels off, stands up and blows a raspberry (9.6-10.8s), force fails through the grab, melt, hat dive and faceplant with giggling eyes (13.5-18.0s), wit wins through the dance, the copy and the stomp (20.5-23.5s), and nightfall adds the button (24.5-28.5s); the slack spot is 16.0-19.8s, about 4s of Pim dizzy and then standing with no clear visible decision.

payoff.note: The ending is deliberate and answers the opening's copycat premise: the shadow is drawn out of the tree's shade copying the dance (21.0-22.0s), creeps to Pim's feet with a side-eye (22.5-23.0s), gets stomped (squeezed-shut eyes at f692), is back attached and mirroring Pim with no eyes (23.5-24.5s), and then after sundown its two white eyes open in the dark and one winks (f816, f835); the risk is that the wink holds only about 20 frames (f835 to the f855 end) before the film cuts.

cause_before_effect.note: Every important cause comes before its effect: the shadow's copying is set up at 0-8s, including Pim's arm test at 7.0-8.0s, before the dance exploits it (21s); the melt into shade (f423-f431) comes before the dive it defeats (f448-f468); Pim's lean and squint (9.0-10.0s) comes before the detach (f288); the sun sinking (24.5-25.5s) comes before the shadows vanish (26.0s); and Pim's worried downward look (26.0-27.0s) comes before the eyes open (f816); weaker links are the idea moment (19.8s), carried only by a sound cue and a raised arm, and the hat that is on the ground at 19.5s and back on Pim's head at 20.0s with no visible pick-up.

clarity_normal_speed.note: Most key poses are legible at phone size (the raspberry tongue in phone-f00333, the crash and dizzy eyes in phone-f00465, the eyes in the shade in phone-f00633, the wink in the f835 strip), but clarity at real speed cannot be established from 0.5s samples; the specific risks are: the dense 9.6-11.6s cluster (detach, stand, recoil, eyes, raspberry and run in 2s); the twin at the right edge at 12.0s and back at the tree on the left at 12.5s, a path not seen in the samples; the lag beat, which depends on reading an upside-down projected shadow pose (5.0-5.8s) while Pim's double-take faces the camera instead of the shadow; a stomp that is only a small hop (f688-f692); and a wink held about 0.67s before the end.
clarity_normal_speed.evidence: strip-stand_up, strip-raspberry, strip-run_off; 12.00s f360 vs 12.50s f375; 5.00s f150 to 6.00s f180; strip-stomp; strip-wink

picture_sound_link.note: Declared not applicable before production: a silent comedy by design, with no narration or dialogue and sound limited to score and effects; the request's narration list is empty, which confirms it.

suggestions: Hold the final wink longer: it starts at f835 and the film ends at f855 (about 0.67s). Add roughly 0.5-1.0s of hold, or a tiny Pim reaction after the wink, so the last laugh is not clipped by the cut or the loop.

Make the turn from force to wit visible: at 19.0-19.8s Pim only raises an arm with a blank look, and the change rests on a chime. Give it a clear 'idea' pose or expression change (brows up, finger up, a glance at the eyes in the shade and then at the sunlit grass) so viewers understand the dance is a trap before it starts.

Make the shadow's oddity unmistakable within the first 1.5s (for example, a visibly late step or sigh during the walk-in). In the stills nothing unusual shows until 5.0s, which is a long time for a scrolling viewer.

Have Pim's double-take at f176 look down at the shadow, not straight out at the camera, so the cause (the shadow's held stretch and flourish at f150-f174) and the reaction are connected in one glance.

Clarify the run-off path: the twin exits the right edge at 12.0s and is standing by the tree on the left at 12.5s. If that is a loop around Pim, make sure it reads at speed, or simplify it to a single dash toward the tree.

Sell the stomp with a bigger anticipation and a firmer landing pose (the hop at f688-f692 is only a few pixels), and show the hat being picked up between 19.5s and 20.0s, or keep it off until a deliberate put-on.
sampling_limits: I judged ordered decoded frames only: a contact sheet every 15 frames (0.5s), eleven dense strips (every 2nd frame, +/-8 frames) around named moments, and six full 360x640 phone frames. I saw no moving playback and heard no audio. Not verifiable: whether the shadow visibly lags 'one beat late' during the walk-in (the core opening hook), the timing and readability of fast actions between samples (the 9.6-11.6s escape cluster, the twin's path at 12.0-12.5s, the 13.4-14.6s chase), how goofy the dance looks in motion, whether the stomp reads as a deliberate stomp, how long the wink feels before the end, and comic timing in general. The sound cues and their alignment are known only from the request's cue table, not from listening. For these reasons clarity_normal_speed is NOT_ASSESSED, and the human phone viewing should check those points.
summary: From frames alone the story is coherent and well built: a copycat shadow is set up (0-8s), breaks free with a clear stand-up and raspberry (9.6-11.6s), beats force by melting into the tree's shade and laughing at Pim's faceplant (14-18s), and is beaten by wit when Pim dances and it cannot resist copying its way back to be stomped into place (20.5-23.5s), with a nightfall wink as the button (27.2-28.5s). Causes precede effects and the payoff answers the premise. I found no blocking story issue. The weak points are a calm opening whose lag hook I could not verify, a thin 'idea' turn at 19.8s, a compressed chase with an unclear run path, and a final wink held only about 0.67s; clarity at real speed must be confirmed by the human viewing.
